chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: When tap got big and when he played the Cotton Club
summary: Tap did not get big until 1926-27, he played the original Cotton Club in 1923-24 and not the later downtown one for years.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, before we get into that, I'd like to ask you just a couple of things about what tap dancing was at this particular time in terms of its popularity. Was it popular dancing?
No, no, tap dancing ain't standing out now. There's just dancing now. Singing and dancing now.
Was tap dancing big up in Harlem?
It wasn't big
When did it become big?
It didn't get big until 1926, '27, I think it was.
And the time you performed in the Cotton Club was about when?
Cotton Club was 1923, '24.
You didn't perform subsequently in future years?
Different places, yeah --
Cotton Club, I mean.
No, no Cotton Club before that.
After that, I mean. Did you perform in the Cotton Club in the '30's?
No, no, no more. I didn't go back there. The Cotton Club opened
downtown after that, later.
How long was it open uptown?
Oh, about two years, two or three years.
That's all. Wasn't it a place that continued --
That's right it continued but that's all it run to me, I never know any longer, I don't know about it.
Any particular reason why you didn't continue to perform there until a certain time?
Well, they were changing shows. They changed shows like all cafes do.
You would think that in future years they would have brought back Buck and Bubbles.
Buck and Bubbles were brought back way later downtown. They used the new Cotton Club so they got Buck and Bubbles
later. After that used Cab Calloway and Ethel Waters and Bill Robinson downtown and didn't get Buck and Bubbles, ain't that something, they didn't go downtown.
